rationale: Verified reviewed commit 44e6cf2f and confirmed my standing APPROVE verdict. The diff is confined to the three disclosed files and four intended corrections: two comment rewording sites in panel_advisory.go, one decision-table label in gate.go, and deletion of the zero-caller residualDirtyPaths helper from complete.go. The rewordings replace present-tense descriptions of complete's retired CommitAll ordering with the delivered materialization ordering without changing runtime behavior; the deleted helper has no surviving references. The disclosed CompleteBead msg != empty auto-commit branch is unreachable from the sole production caller, which always passes an empty message after bead 6 moved materialization upstream. It is inert compatibility surface inside a large shared merge/cleanup function, makes no false documentation claim, and is appropriately deferred to a separately scoped follow-up rather than expanding this final corrective commit.

findings.title: Round-4 fixes are exactly confined
findings.detail: git show 44e6cf2f --stat reports only internal/complete/complete.go, internal/complete/panel_advisory.go, and internal/panel/gate.go (14 insertions, 43 deletions). Full diff inspection confirms two comment rewords, one comment label reword, and deletion of the 31-line residualDirtyPaths function. git diff-tree --check is clean, and git grep finds no residualDirtyPaths reference at the reviewed commit.

findings.title: CompleteBead dead branch may remain outside this bead
findings.detail: The only non-test production invocation is internal/complete/complete.go, which calls CompleteBead with msg empty, so the msg != empty auto-commit branch cannot execute in production today. Removing that branch would alter a public executor seam and a sensitive shared merge/cleanup function while providing no acceptance-criterion behavior change. Deferring the cleanup to a focused follow-up is proportionate; it is not a blocker for bead 6.

findings.title: Prior approval stands
findings.detail: Commit 44e6cf2f changes none of the materialization protocol, gate decisions, state transitions, git operations, or previously verified race closure. The round-2 through round-4 approval basis therefore remains valid.
